problem: Embodied instruction-following agents such as those on ALFRED learn from static corpora of expert demonstrations directly in pixel space. They have no way to reason and learn abstract, multi-step policies interactively in language before acting in the physical world. Purely vision-based agents also overfit to seen rooms and generalize poorly to unseen scenes.
motivation: Humans solve tasks like 'put a washed apple in the fridge' by reasoning abstractly with semantic priors (where objects are, affordances, pre-conditions) before acting. Text environments can supply cheap, programmatic, interactive linguistic feedback with no rendering or physics, which no embodied simulator provides. The authors hypothesize that learning abstract language-based policies through interaction yields priors that transfer to unfamiliar embodied environments.
key_idea: Build ALFWorld, a PDDL-aligned TextWorld twin of each ALFRED/THOR scene. Train a text agent (BUTLER::Brain) interactively with DAgger in the cheap text world, then deploy it zero-shot in the embodied world. A Mask R-CNN detector turns frames into text observations, and an A*/API controller turns its text actions into low-level physical actions.
insight: Interaction is what makes the abstract policy transfer. With the same number of expert episodes, DAgger training beats behavior cloning after zero-shot embodied transfer (All Tasks 19/10 vs Seq2Seq 6/5 SR seen/unseen). Within TextWorld, removing beam-search failure recovery drops All Tasks seen SR from 40 to 19, and removing DAgger drops it further to 10. Training only in text generalizes better to unseen rooms than training in the embodied world: 34.3 vs 23.1 unseen SR with an oracle perception/controller. It is also ~7x faster (6.1 vs 0.9 eps/s), whereas embodied-only training overfits to seen rooms (33.6 seen). A text state space beats visual features: ResNet-18 features score 10.0/6.0 and Mask R-CNN FPN features 11.4/4.5, against BUTLER's 18.8/10.1. The action-only agent scores 0, so memorizing action sequences does not work. Other ablations: token-by-token generation was necessary (candidate-command agents overfit and had zero embodied transfer), and RL from sparse reward failed entirely. The drop from TextWorld (40/35) to Oracle-embodied (37/26) to real perception/navigation (19/10) quantifies the domain gap and the perception/navigation bottleneck.
method: ALFWorld environment: each ALFRED scene is described in PDDL. The TextWorld engine (Fast Downward planner + context-sensitive template grammar) builds an equivalent interactive text game with high-level actions (goto/take/put/open/close/toggle/clean/heat/cool/examine). It covers 6 task types with 3,553 train / 140 seen / 134 unseen tasks, and excludes slicing and portable-container tasks.

BUTLER::Brain text agent: a Transformer seq2seq model. The encoder has 5 conv layers, single-head self-attention and hidden size 64 over frozen 768-d DistilBERT embeddings. A context-query (QANet-style tri-linear) attention aggregates observation and goal, and a GRU carries history. An observation queue (k=5) of recent unique observations is always prefixed with o0, which lists all receptacles. The decoder generates actions token-by-token (max 20 tokens) with a pointer-softmax copy mechanism and tied embeddings.

Imitation learning with DAgger: a rule-based subgoal expert supervises training. Expert assistance is annealed from 100% to 1% over 50K episodes, and transitions are stored in a replay buffer (500K episodes). Updates sample 64 sequences of 4 transitions (2 for burn-in, 2 for update, recurrent-DQN style) every 5 steps; episodes cap at 50 steps and 8 random seeds are run.

Beam-search failure recovery: when an action fails ('Nothing happens'), the agent beam-searches (width 10) and tries the top-5 alternative action sentences in rank order. Otherwise it decodes greedily.

BUTLER::Vision state estimator: a Mask R-CNN (COCO-pretrained, fine-tuned on 50K ALFRED frames, 73 classes) detects objects. Detections are templated into text such as 'On table 1, you see a mug 1, ...' with instance IDs.

BUTLER::Body controller: 'goto' runs A* on a pre-built grid map, where each receptacle has an interaction viewpoint (x, y, yaw, tilt). This outputs MoveAhead/Rotate/Look primitives that are executed open-loop. Manipulation actions call the ALFRED API with the predicted Mask R-CNN mask.

setting.backbone: Custom Transformer seq2seq text agent with pointer softmax and frozen DistilBERT embeddings (trained from scratch with DAgger); Mask R-CNN (COCO-pretrained, fine-tuned on ALFRED frames) as perception; A* planner as controller
setting.training_data: ALFWorld TextWorld training games (3,553 tasks across 6 ALFRED task types, templated goals), trained with DAgger from a rule-based expert for 50K episodes; Mask R-CNN fine-tuned on a 50K-image dataset recorded by replaying ALFRED expert demonstrations. No embodied training for the main agent.
setting.observation: egocentric RGB frames from THOR converted to templated text via Mask R-CNN detections, plus the initial observation o0 listing all receptacles and a templated goal description (no step-by-step instructions)
setting.action_space: generated high-level text commands (goto/take/put/open/close/toggle/clean/heat/cool/examine), each mapped to low-level THOR actions (MoveAhead, RotateLeft/Right, LookUp/Down, Pickup/Put/Open/Close/ToggleOn/Off with masks)
setting.privileged: Pre-built grid map of each scene with receptacle locations and interaction viewpoints (used by A* navigation). The initial observation o0 enumerates all receptacles in the scene. The Oracle variant additionally uses ground-truth object detections and teleport navigation.

numbers_note: ALFWorld is not a canonical benchmark name, so the text version is recorded as other:ALFWorld-Text (the version later LLM-agent papers call 'ALFWorld', 134 unseen games) and the THOR version as other:ALFWorld-Embodied. Both use ALFWorld's own seen (140) and unseen (134) splits, which are drawn from ALFRED's seen/unseen validation data but exclude slicing and portable-container tasks. GC is ALFRED's goal-condition success rate. The paper reports two text-only BUTLER All Tasks figures that disagree slightly because they use different seed selection: the 'Zero-shot Domain Transfer' table's TextWorld column gives seen 40 / unseen 35, whereas the 'Generalization within TextWorld' table gives 40 / 37. The unimodal-baselines table reports embodied BUTLER All Tasks peak performance as 18.8 seen / 10.1 unseen, versus 19 / 10 in the main table. The training-strategy table (oracle perception/controller, peak performance) gives: TW-only 27.1 seen / 34.3 unseen at 6.1 eps/s; Embodied-only 33.6 / 23.1 at 0.9 eps/s; Hybrid 21.4 / 23.1 at 0.7 eps/s. The Seq2Seq behavior-cloning baseline scores 6 (15) seen / 5 (14) unseen embodied, and 10 / 9 in text. Model-ablation results (observation queue length, o0, recurrence, number of training games) are shown only in a figure.
results: Trained only in TextWorld, BUTLER transfers zero-shot to embodied ALFRED scenes with 19% seen / 10% unseen success on All Tasks (GC 31/20). The equally sized behavior-cloning Seq2Seq baseline gets 6/5, and the oracle upper bound (GT detection + teleport) reaches 37/26. In pure text, BUTLER reaches 40/37 SR (greedy BUTLER_g 19/22). TextWorld-only training generalizes better to unseen rooms than embodied-only training (34.3 vs 23.1, with oracle perception/controller) and is ~7x faster. With human-annotated goals, success falls to 8/3.
limitations: Navigation relies on a pre-built grid map with known receptacle locations and interaction viewpoints, and o0 lists all receptacles in the scene; this is a strong privileged prior.

There is a large text-to-embodied domain gap (physical size constraints, Mask R-CNN misdetections, collisions), so absolute embodied success is low (10% unseen). Performance also collapses with human-written goals, since training uses only templated language.

Only a subset of ALFRED is covered (6 task types, no slicing or containers, goal descriptions only), templated state descriptions are used, and RL from sparse reward failed, so the method depends on DAgger with a rule-based expert.
builds_on: Pointer softmax / Transformer seq2seq text agents (Yuan et al. 2018)
compares_to: Seq2Seq behavior cloning from static expert demonstrations
